jobs.occupation: Engineer - Power System Analytics; DK - Fredericia
jobs.description:
Do you want to contribute to the secure and stable operation of the Danish power system as renewable energy continues to grow? You will combine power system engineering, data analytics and applied research to develop methods and tools that support system stability and the management of critical power system events.

Join our power system specialists

At our head office in Fredericia you join a department responsible for supporting the secure and stable operation of the Danish power system, both today and in the future with an increasing share of renewable energy. We develop methods, analyses and digital solutions that support system stability, security of supply and the handling of major disturbances.  As part of Energinet’s System Operations organisation, we work closely with the Control Centre, IT specialists and international transmission system operators.

The department consists of 18 colleagues organised into two groups. Together, we combine knowledge in power system operations, grid analysis, system stability, data analytics, and digital solution development. You become part of an inter-national and collaborative environment where we use both Danish and English in our daily work. 

Develop methods and tools for system stability

You contribute to developing next-generation dynamic stability assessment, system monitoring, and power system restoration capabilities for an electricity system increasingly based on renewable energy. 

Your primary responsibilities include:

• analysing power system dynamics, stability and disturbance events using PowerFactory and PSCAD
• developing and applying methods based on PMU and other operational measurement data
• identifying stability risks and proposing mitigation measures together with operational specialists
• supporting the digitalisation and automation of processes related to Dynamic Stability Assessment
• collaborating with operational specialists, software developers, researchers and external partners across the Nordic and European power sector

“You join a specialised environment where we share knowledge, ask questions and solve complex technical challenges together.”
– Nan Qin, Team Leader

Bring your technical curiosity

You have a relevant background in electrical engineering, power systems or a related technical discipline. You may be newly graduated or have some professional experience. Experience with power system analysis, dynamic simulations, PowerFactory, programming, measurement data or digital tool development is an advantage.

Most importantly, you are curious, structured and keen to learn. You ask questions and seek input when needed, while also taking responsibility for your own analyses. You enjoy teamwork, and you are equally comfortable addressing complex technical questions on your own.

Will you make a difference with us?

We look forward to receiving your motivated CV no later than 8 November. You may want to pencil in a couple of dates in your calendar already. We expect the first interview to take place online on 13 November and the second interview in Fredericia on 19 November.

If you have questions about the job, please contact Thue Søndergård Thomsen, Head of Department, on mail THSTH@energinet.dk.

Special conditions: As Energinet performs tasks critical to society, we carry out background checks prior to employment. Employment is conditional upon your background check being compatible with employment at Energinet. The background check is also carried out once a year.

The position also requires that you are able to obtain and maintain security clearance. On PET's website, you can read more about security clearance.

We see diversity as a strength and encourage all qualified people, regardless of background, to apply for the job. We work actively and determinedly with diversity in Energinet and therefore encourage you to exclude information about age, marital status, etc. to minimise outage biases in the process. You can read more about our diversity policy here.

Energinet Systemsansvar's core tasks are to integrate renewable energy, ensure equal access to the grids, develop market design, monitor, and balance the transmission grid and ensure security of supply in Denmark. We are a subsidiary of the Energinet Group, which represents the interests of society when supplying Denmark with electricity and gas and that the energy system is converted to green energy. Our culture is closely linked to our social responsibility, and we work actively with the UN's global goals on sustainable energy, climate action, partnerships for action as well as industry, innovation, and infrastructure. By leading the way in the green transition, we can help to solve the global climate challenge. New solutions require us to be able to see problems from many different angles, and diversity is therefore a keyword in our culture. We strive to listen to, involve and share our knowledge. Based on the values of courage and trust, we focus on constantly developing ourselves as an organisation and as people. Read more at our website www.energinet.dk.

jobs.occupation: Demand Planner
jobs.description:
Are you structured, analytical, and motivated by ensuring that products are available when our customers need them?

We are looking for a Demand Planner to support the daily planning and replenishment of our warehouse assortment and help ensure the right balance between product availability and inventory.

In this role, you will work hands-on with demand forecasts, replenishment, purchase orders, inventory levels, and planning exceptions. You will be an important link between Sales, Procurement, Warehouse, Operations, and our suppliers and factories, helping turn demand into clear and executable supply requirements.

Your key responsibilities

• 
Maintain and update demand forecasts based on sales history, trends, customer input, and changes in demand.

• 
Plan replenishment and ensure timely ordering of products for our warehouse assortment.

• 
Follow up on open purchase orders, delivery dates, and expected incoming supply.

• 
Monitor stock levels and identify potential shortages, excess inventory, and availability risks.

• 
React to changes in demand and supply and adjust plans accordingly.

• 
Follow up on service level, forecast accuracy, inventory, and other operational planning KPIs.

• 
Work closely with Sales, Procurement, Warehouse, and Operations to resolve day-to-day planning and availability issues.

• 
Maintain high-quality planning parameters and master data.

• 
Support improvements to planning processes, systems, and ways of working.

Who are you?

You have experience within demand planning, replenishment, purchasing, inventory management, or supply chain planning and enjoy working in a role where you are close to the daily operation.

You are comfortable working with numbers, data, and planning systems and have a structured approach to managing priorities and following up on deviations. Experience with ERP systems, forecasting or replenishment tools, and Excel is an advantage.

As a person, you are structured, proactive, persistent, and solution-oriented. You take ownership of your area, follow issues through to resolution, and communicate clearly with colleagues and stakeholders.

What we offer

You will join an international planning organization and take responsibility for an important part of our daily planning operation. Your work will have a direct impact on product availability, inventory levels, and customer service.

You will work closely with colleagues across Sales, Procurement, Logistics, Warehouse, and Operations and have opportunities to develop your competencies within demand and supply chain planning.

jobs.occupation: FRISKSNIT søger medarbejdende teamleder til fødevareproduktion i Hedehusene/FRISKSNIT is hiring a Hands-on Team Leader for Food Production in Hedehusene, Denmark
jobs.description:
DANSK:

Timelønnet fuldtidsstilling på 37 timer om ugen – med faste arbejdstider søndag–torsdag og fri fredag–lørdag.

Har du øje for kvalitet, kan du holde overblik, og har du lyst til at tage ansvar for et mindre team? Så søger vi dig til vores fødevareproduktion i Hedehusene.

Hos FRISKSNIT søger vi en medarbejdende teamleder, som både deltager i det praktiske produktionsarbejde og koordinerer opgaverne for tre kolleger. Du skal sammen med teamet sikre, at produkterne bliver pakket korrekt, mærket rigtigt og færdige til tiden.

Vi er en fødevareproduktionsvirksomhed med cirka 75 fuldtidsansatte. Vi er medlem af Dansk Industri og omfattet af Industriens Overenskomst.

Dine arbejdsopgaver

Du bliver ansvarlig for den daglige koordinering i dit team og samarbejder tæt med den produktionsansvarlige. Du deltager selv i produktionen og følger op på, at teamet arbejder effektivt og overholder instruktionerne for kvalitet, hygiejne og sikkerhed.

Dine vigtigste opgaver er at:

• 
Koordinere og fordele arbejdet mellem teamets tre øvrige medarbejdere og følge op på dagens opgaver og effektivitet.

• 
Sikre korrekt pakning og mærkning, herunder kontrollere emballage, etiketter og datomærkning.

• 
Deltage i produktions- og pakkearbejdet samt støtte og oplære kolleger i de aftalte arbejdsgange.

• 
Reagere på fejl og forsinkelser og inddrage den produktionsansvarlige, når der er behov for hjælp eller ændrede prioriteringer.

Hvem er du?

Du arbejder omhyggeligt, tager ansvar og bevarer overblikket, når der er travlt. Du kan give tydelige instruktioner og bidrager til et godt samarbejde gennem en respektfuld og hjælpsom tilgang til dine kolleger.

Erfaring fra fødevareproduktion, pakkeri eller lignende er en fordel, men du behøver ikke have en bestemt faguddannelse. Erfaring med koordinering af opgaver eller oplæring af kolleger er også en fordel. Det er ikke et krav, at du tidligere har haft titlen teamleder.

Arbejdssproget er engelsk. Du skal derfor kunne forstå arbejdsinstruktioner og kommunikere tydeligt med kolleger og ledelse på engelsk.

Arbejdstid:

Stillingen er på 37 betalte arbejdstimer om ugen med følgende faste mødetider:

Søndag: kl. 08.00–16.00
Mandag–torsdag: kl. 12.00–20.00
Fredag og lørdag: fri

Mødetiderne omfatter samlet tre timers ubetalte pauser om ugen. Pauserne indgår ikke i de 37 betalte arbejdstimer. Den konkrete placering af pauserne fremgår af arbejdsplanen.

Arbejdstidens placering følger virksomhedens lokalaftale.

Løn og ansættelsesvilkår:

Du bliver timelønnet med grundtimeløn, et fast teamledertillæg og relevante tillæg, herunder tillæg for søndagsarbejde.

Ansættelsen sker efter Industriens Overenskomst og virksomhedens gældende lokalaftaler, med pension, feriepenge og fritvalg.

Fritvalg og søgnehelligdagsbidrag udbetales månedligt sammen med lønnen efter virksomhedens aftale.

Du får oplæring i arbejdsopgaverne, vores produkter og de kvalitetskrav, der gælder i produktionen. Du får en praktisk rolle med ansvar for den daglige koordinering og tæt samarbejde med både dit team og den produktionsansvarlige.

Ansættelsesform: Tidsubegrænset fuldtidsansættelse.
Arbejdssted: FRISKSNIT, Hedelykken 14, 2640 Hedehusene.
Tiltrædelse: Efter aftale.

Sådan søger du

Send dit CV og en kort ansøgning til Job@frisksnit.dk senest fredag den 13. november 2026. Skriv ”Teamleder – FRISKSNIT” i emnefeltet.

Fortæl gerne om din erfaring med produktion, pakning eller koordinering af kolleger, og hvorfor du er interesseret i stillingen. Du er velkommen til at skrive din ansøgning på engelsk.

Spørgsmål til stillingen kan også sendes til Job@frisksnit.dk.

Vi opfordrer alle kvalificerede ansøgere til at søge stillingen.

Permanent, hourly-paid position with 37 paid working hours per week – fixed working hours Sunday to Thursday, with Fridays and Saturdays off.

Do you have an eye for quality, enjoy organising daily tasks and want to take responsibility for a small team? Join our food production team in Hedehusene.

At FRISKSNIT, we are looking for a hands-on Team Leader who will take part in production while coordinating the work of three colleagues. Together with your team, you will ensure that products are packed correctly, labelled accurately and ready on time.

You will coordinate your team’s daily work and work closely with the person responsible for production. You will also take part in production yourself, helping the team work efficiently and follow our quality, hygiene and safety procedures.

Your main tasks will be to:

Coordinate and allocate tasks among the three other team members and follow up on daily work and productivity.

• 
Ensure correct packing and labelling, including checking packaging, labels and date markings.

• 
Take part in production and packing, while supporting colleagues and training them in the agreed procedures.

•

About you

You work carefully, take responsibility and stay organised when things get busy. You can give clear instructions and contribute to good teamwork by treating your colleagues with respect and offering support.

Experience in food production, packing or a similar role is an advantage, but no specific vocational qualification is required. Experience coordinating tasks or training colleagues is also an advantage. You do not need to have held a Team Leader position before.

The position offers 37 paid working hours per week, with the following fixed schedule:

Sunday: 08:00–16:00
Monday–Thursday: 12:00–20:00
Friday and Saturday: Days off

The scheduled hours include a total of three hours of unpaid breaks per week. Breaks are not included in the 37 paid working hours. Break times are specified in the work schedule.

Working hours are arranged under the company’s local agreement.

This is an hourly-paid position with a basic hourly wage, a fixed Team Leader allowance and applicable supplements, including a supplement for Sunday work.

Employment is covered by the Danish Industrial Agreement (Industriens Overenskomst) and the company’s applicable local agreements, including pension contributions, holiday pay and flexible benefits.

Flexible benefits payments (fritvalg) and the public-holiday allowance are paid monthly together with wages under the company’s agreement.

You will receive training in your tasks, our products and the quality requirements that apply in production. The role combines practical work with responsibility for daily coordination and close cooperation with your team and the person responsible for production.

Employment type: Permanent, full-time employment with no fixed end date.
Workplace: FRISKSNIT, Hedelykken 14, 2640 Hedehusene, Denmark.

How to apply

Please send your CV and a short application to Job@frisksnit.dk by Friday, 13 November 2026. Use “Team Leader – FRISKSNIT” as the email subject.

Tell us about your experience in production, packing or coordinating colleagues, and why you are interested in the position. Applications in English are welcome.

Questions about the position can also be sent to Job@frisksnit.dk.

We welcome applications from all qualified candidates.

jobs.description:

RENTEQ Automotive is looking for two software people who are curious, learn fast and want to try their hand at a bit of everything. You do not need to be a specialist or have many years of experience. What matters most is that you are adaptable and eager to learn.

About RENTEQ

RENTEQ Automotive is a Danish company at the forefront of electrifying existing diesel machines and vehicles. We convert everything from vans to dumpers and excavators, and all the vehicles run on control software we develop ourselves. We are a growing startup with short decision paths, a small team, and our workshop and offices under one roof in Dragør.

What is it like to work with us?

Our software developers are never far from the product. The workshop is right next door, and the changes you make in the morning can be tested in a vehicle in the afternoon. We are a small team where everyone helps each other, and you will quickly work closely with engineers, mechanics and management.

We do not expect you to know everything from day one. You will get time to learn our system, and support from colleagues working with CAN, embedded software, high voltage and testing. In return, we expect you to be curious, ask questions and be keen to get stuck in.

The job

You will start by getting to know our system: how the vehicles are controlled, how the software is structured, and how it all ties together with CAN and hardware. After that, you will become part of the daily software work and help develop the system further. Our control software is currently built in Simulink, and we are moving parts of it to C/C++, so you will work with both.

Your tasks will include:

•       Get to know our control software and how it works together with the vehicle

•       Flash and test software on the bench and in the vehicles

•       Test new components and help integrate them into the system

•       Debug using CAN logs and measurement data

•       Help develop new features and improve existing ones

•       Document what you learn and build so the rest of the team can use it too.

•       Programming experience, for example C, C++, Python or Matlab

•       Curious, adaptable and quick to learn new things

•       You enjoy hands on work and seeing things work in real life

•       Good English skills, Danish is an advantage

•       Simulink or Stateflow

•       Embedded software or microcontrollers

•       CAN bus and tools such as PCAN or Vector

•       Electric vehicles, batteries or high voltage systems

•       Git.

What we offer

•       A job where you see your software running in real vehicles on the road and on construction sites

•       A fast-paced professional development opportunity with broad insight into software, hardware and electric vehicles

•       A small, informal team where asking questions and helping each other comes naturally

•       Varied tasks on many different vehicles and machines

•       The opportunity to grow with the company and shape how we build our software going forward

•       Workshop and offices in Dragør with easy access by car or public transport.

jobs.occupation: PhD fellowship/scholarship, Integrating Hormonal and Biomechanical Stimuli in Multi-scale Modelling of human Vascular cells
jobs.employer_name: Technical Sciences - Institut for Mekanik og Produ
jobs.description:
Applicants are invited for a PhD fellowship/scholarship at Graduate School of Technical Sciences, Aarhus University, Denmark, within the Mechanical and Production Engineering programme. The position is available from 01 March 2027 or later. You can submit your application via the link under 'how to apply'.

Title:
Integrating Hormonal and Biomechanical Stimuli in Multi-scale Modelling of human Vascular cells

Research area and project description:
As part of the ERC Starting Grant project DISSEX, which aims at developing a sex-aware multiscale framework to predict vascular dissection risk, we are looking for a highly motivated PhD candidate to join our multi-disciplinary Cardiovascular Engineering (CareEng) group at Aarhus University. This PhD project specifically aims at quantifying how human coronary arteries respond to systemic hormonal fluctuations and biomechanical stress through both experimental and computational techniques. There are 2 objectives.

Objective 1: Experimental investigation of vascular adaptation
The candidate will use innovative microfluidic platforms and ex vivo human coronary arteries to recreate physiological and pathological vascular environments. By exposing vascular tissues to controlled flow, pressure, and hormone profiles representative of daily fluctuations in estradiol, cortisol, and testosterone, the project will quantify how endothelial and smooth muscle cells respond in terms of proliferation, apoptosis, signalling, and biomechanical function. Particular attention will be given to endothelial pathways involving nitric oxide and endothelin-1, providing a unique dataset on how systemic and mechanical stimuli jointly influence vascular health.

Objective 2: Development of a multiscale computational model
Building on the experimental findings, the candidate will develop a multiscale computational framework linking cellular activity to vessel-scale biomechanics. Combining agent-based modelling with computational fluid dynamics, the model will integrate hormonal regulation, cellular adaptation, and biomechanical stresses within the vascular wall. The resulting digital platform will enable mechanistic investigation of vascular remodelling processes and provide a foundation for understanding conditions that may predispose arteries to dissection.

The PhD candidate will join an interdisciplinary team bringing together expertise in vascular physiology, Cardiovascular biomechanics, microfluidics and fabrication; computational modelling, and clinical cardiovascular medicine. The project includes close collaboration with clinicians, biologists, and engineers and provides access to state-of-the-art laboratory and computational research facilities.

Qualifications and specific competences:
We are looking for highly motivated and independent candidates with the intention to complete a 3-year PhD at Aarhus University. The ideal candidate is expected to have most of the following qualifications:
 
• Master’s degree in Biomedical Engineering, Biomechanical Engineering, Biotechnology or relevant fields.
• In-depth knowledge in fluid mechanics and cardiovascular applications.
• Experience with cell culture and tissue engineering
• Familiarity with numerical modelling (CFD), and software such as COMSOL, SimVascular, or similar software
• (optional) Previous exposure to agent-based modelling or systems biology
• excellent written and spoken English (optional Danish).

Place of employment and place of work:
The place of employment is Aarhus University, and the place of work is Department of Mechanical and Production Engineering, Aarhus University, Katrinebjergvej 89F, 8200 Aarhus N.

The position starts on April 1, 2027, and will terminate at the end of the appointment period unless otherwise agreed.

Beskrivelse til interne kandidater

The Research Unit of General Practice at the Institute of Public Health, University of Southern Denmark (SDU), invites applications for a 2-year full time Assistant Professor position in Global Health.

The position starts on April 1, 2027, and will terminate at the end of the appointment period unless otherwise agreed.

Job Description
The position involves research in global health with a particular focus on strengthening primary healthcare systems for vulnerable and underserved populations in low- and middle-income countries. The successful candidate will contribute to the international research project STRENGTHENing Gender-Responsive Health Systems for Addressing Non-Communicable Diseases in Climate-Affected Fishing Communities in Western Kenya (STRENGTHEN) and other upcoming global health projects. The STRENGTHEN project aims to improve the prevention and management of NCDs in climate-affected fishing communities in Western Kenya by making the health systems even more gender-responsive. The project will generate evidence on how community health promoters (CHPs) provide NCD care in FEDCs affected by climate change. It will address five key health systems building blocks: health information systems, health workforce, health service, medical technology, and policy and governance. The work will involve conducting implementation and health services research, and collaborating with researchers, healthcare professionals, policymakers, and community stakeholders across different country settings. The position involves travel to Kenya for short periods.

We offer a challenging position in a stimulating research environment with excellent opportunities for collaboration within SDU and with international research partners.

Expectations of qualifications
The successful applicant should have:

• 
A PhD degree (or equivalent) in Global Health, Public Health, Epidemiology, Health Services Research, Implementation Science, or a related discipline

• 
A strong background in health systems research, primary healthcare, chronic disease prevention and management, or health equity research in low- and middle-income countries

• 
A strong academic record

• 
Good collaboration and communication skills

• 
Interest in co-supervising BSc, MSc and PhD students

Following qualifications are preferred:

• 
Experience with mixed-methods research, including qualitative and quantitative data collection and analysis

• 
Experience with implementation science, intervention development, and evaluation of community-based health programmes

• 
Experience with global health research conducted in low- and middle-income countries and/or humanitarian settings

• 
Experience with stakeholder engagement and collaboration with healthcare providers, communities, and policymakers

• 
Experience with writing research applications

• 
Experience in teaching and education

Further information
For further information please contact Prof. Jens Søndergaard, jsondergaard@health.sdu.dk, or Associate Prof. Trine Thilsing, tthilsing@health.sdu.dk 

Application deadline and interviews
The application deadline is November15th 2026 at 11:59 PM/23:59 (CET/CEST)  

Terms of employment 
Appointment as an assistant professor is temporary and for an initial 2-year period, and the preferred start date is from 1. April 2027.

During employment, the assistant professor will complete the Lecturer Training Programme, if this has not already been completed.   

Appointment as an assistant professor requires academic qualifications at PhD level. 

Further information on the appointment procedure can be found in the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Universities. 

The appointment is in accordance with the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations .

Salary is determined in accordance with the applicable collective agreement and based on objective and gender-neutral criteria, including the content of the position, responsibilities, and qualification requirements. As an applicant, you are entitled to information about the starting salary and salary range for the position. This information will be provided during the recruitment process. SDU does not collect information on applicants’ previous salary. Further information on salary and taxation.  

Persons employed in the position may, based on a specific individual managerial assessment, be exempted from time registration, also known as a “self-organizer”. 

Application 
Applications must be submitted electronically using the link “Apply now” - see below.  

We strongly recommend that you read How to apply for a position at SDU before you apply.  

Only applications written in English will be accepted for evaluation.  

Your application must include the following as PDF files:

a motivation letter.

a detailed CV.  

• 
degree certificates (including a Ph.D.-diploma). 

• 
a complete and numbered list of publications.  

• 
3 to 5 scientific peer-reviewed publications considered by the candidate as most important for this position. Please note that a copy of each publication must be attached as a pdf file.

• 
a teaching portfolio detailing the candidate’s prior teaching experience, teaching skills, and teaching philosophy.

Please note that all the above-mentioned information must be included in the application.

Applications received after the deadline and/or incomplete applications will not be considered. 

If you experience technical problems, you must contact hcm-support@sdu.dk.

Assessment and selection process 
Shortlisting will be used as part of the initial selection process. 

Assessment of shortlisted applications will be done under the existing Appointment Order for universities. Shortlisted applications will be assessed by an assessment committee. The committee may request additional information, and, if so, it is the responsibility of the applicant to provide the necessary material. 

When the assessment committee has submitted its report, the applicants will receive part of the evaluation that concerns themselves. 

References will be obtained for the preferred candidate from their current and previous employers. Applicants invited for interview should expect to complete a work-related personality assessment.

Interviews and tests may be part of the overall evaluation. 

About Us
The Research Unit of General Practice is a collaboration between the Research Unit of General Practice in Odense-Esbjerg, which is organizationally affiliated with the Foundation for General Practice Research (FEA), and the Research Unit of General Practice at the Department of Public Health, University of Southern Denmark (SDU).

The primary objective of the Research Unit is to contribute to the improvement and development of health and healthcare for patients, with a particular focus on services provided in and around general practice. 

A cornerstone of our educational activities is the training of Master's and PhD students. In addition, we contribute to teaching across a range of health sciences bachelor's and master's degree programmes at the Faculty of Health Sciences, University of Southern Denmark, as well as within the Research Training Programme of the specialist training programme in general practice.

Further information about The Faculty of Health Sciences. 

Living and working in Denmark

jobs.description:
About Userlink

Userlink runs AI agents in production at several hundred Nordic webshops, including Bahne, XL-BYG, Coolshop and Bygma. The agents handle the customer dialogue before and after the purchase, and every conversation ends up as structured data on demand and purchase barriers. The team is based in Odense.

The brain

The agents are the arms. The next layer is a system that brings together every signal about a webshop and its customers: conversations on chat, email, phone and social, on-site behaviour, orders, returns and reviews.

The system identifies the moments where a sale is won or lost and intervenes while the session is still live. It scores answer coverage per product and closes the gaps, quantifies objections and unmet demand, and traces returns back to the expectation that broke.

Learning happens across all webshops, more than six million visits a month, where patterns become visible that no single shop has the traffic to see. Every intervention is measured against a control group. The patterns are shared, the data stays with each shop.

The hard problems are retrieval and evaluation of LLM output at scale, data isolation when patterns are shared across customers, latency in real-time flows, and attribution that holds up under scrutiny.

The stack

Java with Spring Boot, React and MongoDB, with language models and vector search on top. Moving the backend to C# and .NET is under consideration.

The role

You are one of the first engineers on the brain and own parts of it from idea to production: data model, retrieval, evaluation and the real-time flows that intervene in the session. You write the code yourself, ship it and follow it when it meets real customers.

The work is not split into tickets in advance. You help decide what gets built, and how, and your choices become the foundation the next engineers build on.

Decisions are made on arguments, not titles. Ideas get challenged regardless of where they come from, and the best one wins.

Why founding

You come in while the brain is taking shape. There is no finished architecture to follow, and the choices you make now are the ones everyone after you builds on.

That is why the role comes with equity. You help build the company, and you own part of what you build. In return we expect you to take responsibility like a co-owner, also when things are unclear or go wrong.

Profile

• 
Experience building and running SaaS systems in production

• 
Solid backend experience in Java or C#, and comfortable in React

• 
Has built LLM-based features and knows how to measure whether they work

• 
Owns what they build, also when it breaks in production

• 
AI-assisted development as part of the daily workflow

The person

• 
Dreams of owning and building a company

• 
Ideally has tried starting something and knows what it takes

• 
Thinks like a founder, not an employee

• 
Happily gives more than a regular job asks for, because it is fun

• 
Says things as they are, and can take the same in return

• 
Takes ownership and looks for solutions rather than excuses

• 
Curious, learns fast and has a positive mindset

What we offer

• 
Competitive salary

• 
Equity

• 
Short decision paths and a high degree of technical freedom

• 
Office at Storms Pakhus in Odense

Application process

We take the time it takes to find the right match.

• 
Introductory conversation

• 
Technical test

• 
Conversation about expectations and terms

Send a short description of something you built from scratch and put into production, and what you learned when it met real users, to jobs@userlink.ai.

A position as postdoc (100% time) is vacant at the Research Unit of Child and Adolescent Psychiatry, the Department of Clinical Research, Faculty of Health Sciences, University of Southern Denmark. The position is limited to three years. The starting date is 01 February 2027 or later by agreement and depending on the candidate’s preferences.

We are seeking a researcher with documented experience in epidemiological research who can independently plan studies, conduct analyses and write scientific papers. We are looking for a future colleague with a clear academic interest in women’s mental health and the motivation to develop their research in this field. Experience in psychiatric epidemiology is a distinct advantage.

The project

The position is funded by a grant from the Wellcome Trust through PROMIS, an international research project on women’s mental health during perimenopause. The project is in its initial phase and will draw on cohort data linked to national registers, in collaboration with researchers in the UK, the USA and Sweden.

The project investigates risk factors for the onset or recurrence of depression, anxiety, bipolar disorder and psychotic disorders during perimenopause. The work includes epidemiological studies of risk, the development and validation of prediction models, and studies of hormone therapy and mental health outcomes using target trial emulation.

Research tasks

The postdoc will work closely with Principal Investigator Professor Trine Munk-Olsen and the project’s data analyst and participate actively in the international research collaboration. The candidate will have considerable scope to shape research questions, the structure of individual studies, study designs and methodological choices within the framework of the project.

The main tasks are to:

• 
Plan and conduct epidemiological studies using register and cohort data, including preparing study protocols and analysis plans.

• 
Independently perform statistical analyses, interpret results and write scientific papers.

• 
Identify risk factors for mental disorders during perimenopause and contribute to the development and validation of prediction models.

• 
Contribute to studies using target trial emulation to investigate hormone therapy and mental health outcomes.

• 
Together with other project team members, contribute to applications for access to external datasets and to the maintenance, quality assurance, harmonisation and documentation of the datasets used.

• 
Participate in subprojects and undertake tasks within the international collaboration, including coordination, organising project meetings and following up on joint agreements.

The position will involve limited travel. It is primarily research-oriented. Teaching and supervision duties may be included, depending also on the candidate’s interests and preferences.

Expectations of qualifications

The applicant who is hired must have a Ph.D. degree in epidemiology, health sciences, biostatistics or data science with a strong focus on health. Candidates who have not yet completed their Ph.D. may apply if they expect to obtain the degree by the starting date. However, we envisage that, in addition to their Ph.D., the candidate will have at least 1–2 years of research-related experience, for example as a postdoc, research assistant or statistician.

The applicant must have the following qualifications:

• 
A clear academic interest in research on women’s mental health, including the relationships between reproductive life stages and mental disorders.

• 
First authorship of several scientific papers, including documented experience in epidemiological research based on register or cohort data.

• 
Documented experience with advanced epidemiological and statistical methods.

• 
Documented experience and competence in statistical programming, for example in R or Stata.

• 
A documented ability to independently plan studies, prepare study protocols, conduct analyses and write scientific papers.

• 
Good collaboration skills and the ability to take responsibility for tasks and contribute constructively to joint research projects.

• 
The ability to work systematically with data quality, documentation and the maintenance of research data.

• 
Fluency in written and spoken English.

The following would be an advantage but are not requirements:

•

•

•

•

• 
Written and spoken Danish, as Danish is the working language of the research unit.

Research environment

The position is based in the Research Unit of Child and Adolescent Psychiatry, a growing, dynamic and collaborative research environment at the Department of Clinical Research, University of Southern Denmark. Our research group brings together expertise in psychiatry, psychology, epidemiology and public health. We offer a friendly, inclusive and interdisciplinary working environment where early-career researchers are supported in developing their academic and professional skills. The unit leads several major research projects focusing on perinatal mental health, child and adolescent psychiatry, and early intervention and prevention.

Research strategy for OUH and the Department of Clinical Research

The joint research strategy for the Department of Clinical Research and Odense University Hospital sets the direction for our shared research efforts in the years ahead. Rooted in the vision –We conduct research together to shape the patient care of the future – it focuses in particular on: cross-disciplinary research – with people at the centre; strong research environments – as drivers of development; and the research journey – from idea to impact. jobs.occupation: PhD scholarship in Theoretical Metamaterial Acoustofluidics - DTU Physics
jobs.description:
A 3-year PhD scholarship, starting 1 January 2027 is available in the Department of Physics (DTU Physics) in the field of theoretical metamaterial acoustofluidics supervised by Professor Henrik Bruus, www.staff.dtu.dk/bruus. 

We study the fundamental physics of fluids embedded in elastic solids particularly in the form of metamaterials and actuated by ultrasound through electromechanical transducers. We develop physical models and perform high-fidelity numerical simulations of selected systems often in international collaborations with various experimental groups. The PhD scholarship is part of the theoretical acoustofluidics project "High-performance, metamaterial-based acoustofluidc devices" funded by Independent Research Fund Denmark (DFF-FTP). The main research topics are microscale acoustofluidics, elastodynamics, electromechanical actuation, suppression of viscous dissipation by synchronous fluid-wall motion, acoustic resonances in microdevices, acoustic forces on suspended particles and solutions, and acoustic streaming.

Responsibilities and qualifications
You will be responsible for 

• developing physical models of acoustofluidic devices with metamaterial walls 
• implementing and performing weak-form FEM simulations of metamaterial acoustofluidic devices
• designing, and numerically testing, optimal metamaterial-based devices for high-performance acoustofluidic nanoparticle handling
We expect that you

• create and critically validate acoustofluidics models relevant for your research project, 
• deliver theoretical and modeling results of high quality,
• participate in team work with independent and original theory/modeling contributions,
• collaborate effectively with experimentalists among the international collaborators, 
• are excited to teach and to learn from other group members,
• communicate your insights and results effectively both orally and in writing,
• work with an outstanding drive and enthusiasm.
You must have a two-year master's degree (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree.

Approval and Enrolment 
The scholarship for the PhD degree is subject to academic approval, and the candidate will be enrolled in one of the general degree programmes at DTU. For information about our enrolment requirements and the general planning of the PhD study programme, please see DTU's rules for the PhD education. 

Assessment
The assessment of the applicants will be made by Professor Henrik Bruus.

We offer
DTU is a leading technical university globally recognized for the excellence of its research, education, innovation and scientific advice. We offer a rewarding and challenging job in an international environment. We strive for academic excellence in an environment characterized by collegial respect and academic freedom tempered by responsibility.

Salary and appointment terms 
The appointment will be based on the collective agreement with the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Please see DTU’s salary structure for scientific staff: www.inside.dtu.dk/en/human-resources/during-employment/salary/salary-structures.

The period of employment is 3 years. Starting date is 1 January 2027 (or according to mutual agreement). The position is a full-time position.

You can read more about career paths at DTU here.

Further information
Further information may be obtained from Professor Henrik Bruus, bruus@fysik.dtu.dk. 

You can read more about the research group of Professor Bruus at www.staff.dtu.dk/bruus and about DTU Department of Physics at www.fysik.dtu.dk.

If you are applying from abroad, you may find useful information on working in Denmark and at DTU at DTU – Moving to Denmark. Furthermore, you have the option of joining our monthly free seminar “PhD relocation to Denmark and startup “Zoom” seminar” for all questions regarding the practical matters of moving to Denmark and working as a PhD at DTU. 

Application procedure 
Your complete online application must be submitted no later than 6 November 2026 (23:59 Danish time). Applications must be submitted as one PDF file containing all materials to be given consideration. To apply, please open the link "Apply now", fill out the online application form, and attach all your materials in English in one PDF file. The file must include:

• A letter motivating the application (cover letter)
• Curriculum vitae 
• Grade transcripts and BSc/MSc diploma (in English) including official description of grading scale
You may apply prior to obtaining your master's degree but cannot begin before having received it.

Applications received after the deadline will not be considered.

All interested candidates irrespective of age, gender, disability, race, religion or ethnic background are encouraged to apply. As DTU works with research in critical technology, which is subject to special rules for security and export control, open-source background checks may be conducted on qualified candidates for the position.

At DTU Physics, we perform research, teaching, and innovation in experimental and theoretical physics with the overall aim to benefit society. We contribute to the transition to sustainable energy via research and innovation in catalysis, Power-to-X, and nuclear energy solutions. We design and develop new functional materials, contribute to advances in geosciences and life sciences, and we develop and exploit quantum physics and quantum technologies

Through research and education at an international top level, we create solutions to the major societal challenges of our time and help secure Europe's global leadership in sustainable technological development. Since Hans Christian Ørsted founded DTU almost 200 years ago, our mission has remained the same: We develop and create value through the natural and technical sciences for the benefit of society. jobs.occupation: Postdoctoral Researcher in Mass Spectrometry and Proteomics Technology Development
jobs.description:
Applications are invited for a two-year postdoctoral position in mass spectrometry and proteomics technology development at the Department of Molecular Biology and Genetics (MBG), Aarhus University, Denmark.

The position is available in the Nielsen Laboratory, which focuses on developing advanced mass spectrometry-based technologies to understand regulatory protein states, post-translational modifications (PTMs), and cellular signalling.

We are seeking an ambitious and technically skilled researcher with demonstrated experience in developing, establishing, or optimizing mass spectrometry-based proteomics methodologies. Candidates should have a strong background in at least one area of proteomics technology development, including LC-MS/MS method development, chromatographic optimization, sample preparation, PTM analysis, or related analytical technologies.

The position offers an exciting opportunity to pursue innovative technology development while taking an active role in building and shaping a growing research group at Aarhus University.

Expected start date and duration of employment

The position is a two-year postdoctoral appointment with the possibility of extension.
The expected start date is 15 January 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter.

Job description
The successful candidate will join a growing research programme focused on developing advanced mass spectrometry-based proteomics technologies and applying these to fundamental questions in molecular and cellular biology.

Our research integrates state-of-the-art mass spectrometry, quantitative proteomics, analytical method development, peptide and protein chemistry, and PTM biology to investigate how regulatory protein states control cellular function.

A central objective of the position is to develop innovative analytical methodologies that expand the capabilities, sensitivity, robustness, and throughput of modern proteomics. Potential research directions include advanced LC-MS/MS acquisition strategies, quantitative PTM proteomics, chromatographic optimization, automated sample preparation, and novel approaches for studying protein regulation.

The position provides considerable scientific freedom to develop and pursue new technological ideas, with opportunities to establish independent research directions and translate methodological innovations into high-impact scientific publications.

As an early member of a newly established research group at Aarhus University, the successful candidate will also have a unique opportunity to actively contribute to the development of the laboratory's scientific activities, technological capabilities, and future research directions.

Primary responsibilities

• Develop, establish, and optimize innovative mass spectrometry-based proteomics methodologies.
• Design and independently drive research projects with a strong emphasis on analytical innovation and technological advancement.
• Explore and implement new approaches to improve proteomics sensitivity, quantitative accuracy, reproducibility, and analytical throughput.
• Develop and apply advanced proteomics technologies to investigate PTMs and regulatory protein states.
• Contribute to establishing new experimental workflows and analytical capabilities within the laboratory.
• Collaborate with national and international research partners across proteomics, analytical chemistry, and molecular biology.
• Communicate research findings through publications in leading international scientific journals and presentations at scientific conferences.
• Contribute to the scientific development and continued expansion of the research group, including mentoring junior researchers and developing new collaborative projects.
Your profile
Applicants must hold a PhD in proteomics, analytical chemistry, biochemistry, molecular biology, biotechnology, or a closely related discipline.

We are particularly interested in candidates who have demonstrated the ability to develop, establish, or substantially improve experimental and analytical methodologies, rather than solely applying established proteomics workflows.

Applicants must demonstrate significant hands-on experience and scientific contributions in at least one of the following areas:

• Mass spectrometry method development: Establishment or optimization of advanced LC-MS/MS acquisition methodologies, including data-independent acquisition (DIA), fragmentation strategies, instrument parameter optimization, or related approaches for improving analytical performance on modern mass spectrometry platforms.
• Liquid chromatography and separation technologies: Development and optimization of chromatographic methodologies for proteomics, including LC gradient design, peptide separation, nanoLC or microflow LC, improved peak capacity, or approaches to enhance sensitivity, robustness, and throughput.
• Proteomics sample preparation and workflow development: Development or substantial optimization of protein and peptide sample preparation methodologies, including automated or high-throughput workflows, digestion strategies, sample clean-up, enrichment techniques, or quantitative proteomics applications.
• Post-translational modification proteomics: Development and optimization of methodologies for PTM enrichment, characterization, or quantitative analysis, including phosphorylation, ADP-ribosylation, ubiquitination, or other regulatory protein modifications.
• Peptide and protein chemistry: Development of innovative approaches involving peptide or protein chemistry, chemical modification, affinity enrichment, selective capture, or related analytical strategies relevant to mass spectrometry-based proteomics.
• Innovative proteomics technologies: Development of other advanced analytical approaches, such as low-input or single-cell proteomics, alternative fragmentation techniques, novel sample processing technologies, or integrated analytical workflows.
Expertise in one of these areas is sufficient. Applicants are not expected to possess experience across all the listed technologies. We particularly welcome researchers with a strong technical specialization who are motivated to expand their expertise into complementary areas of proteomics technology development.

Demonstrated scientific achievements
A central selection criterion will be the applicant's demonstrated contribution to methodological development and technological innovation.

Applicants are expected to document relevant expertise through at least one first-author research publication in which they have made a substantial contribution to the development, establishment, or optimization of an analytical method or experimental technology.

In their application, candidates should identify the publication(s) most relevant to this requirement and briefly describe their personal contributions, the technological challenge addressed, and the methodological advances achieved.

Additional qualifications
Experience in one or more of the following areas will be considered an advantage but is not required:

• Proteomics data processing, bioinformatics, quantitative data analysis, or systems biology.
• Advanced computational analysis of LC-MS/MS data, including DIA data processing and statistical evaluation.
• Mammalian cell culture, including experimental perturbations and cellular model systems.
• Handling and processing of biological tissues, clinical samples, or other complex biological materials.
• Development or implementation of laboratory automation and high-throughput experimental workflows.
• Protein biochemistry, molecular biology, or functional studies of protein regulation.
• Programming, scripting, or computational workflow development, including R or Python.
• Experience working across interdisciplinary projects involving analytical technology development and biological applications.
 
Personal qualifications
We are looking for a researcher who:

• Is scientifically ambitious, highly motivated, and driven by developing innovative solutions to challenging analytical problems.
• Demonstrates creativity, initiative, and a strong ability to translate scientific ideas into experimental advances.
• Takes ownership of research projects and has the determination to drive them from initial concept to publication.
• Enjoys solving technical challenges and continuously improving experimental methodologies.
• Thrives in a dynamic research environment where new ideas, technologies, and scientific directions are actively developed.
• Works independently while contributing positively to a collaborative and supportive research environment.
• Has strong scientific communication skills and an interest in developing an independent research profile.

Who we are
The position will be based in the Nielsen Laboratory at the Department of Molecular Biology and Genetics (MBG), Aarhus University.

Our research focuses on understanding how dynamic post-translational modification networks regulate protein function and cellular behaviour. We develop and apply innovative mass spectrometry-based technologies to characterize regulatory protein states and uncover fundamental mechanisms controlling cellular function in health and disease.

The laboratory builds on more than 15 years of internationally recognized research in regulatory proteomics, ADP-ribosylation biology, and mass spectrometry-based technology development.

We are currently establishing and expanding our research activities at Aarhus University, combining technological innovation with fundamental biological discovery.

Joining the laboratory at this stage provides a particularly attractive opportunity for a motivated researcher to help build a research environment, influence its technological development, establish new analytical capabilities, and contribute to defining future research priorities.

The group benefits from strong international scientific connections and an interdisciplinary research environment spanning molecular biology, genome stability, structural biology, enzymology, and advanced proteomics.

MBG provides an outstanding interdisciplinary research environment with state-of-the-art infrastructure and a strong commitment to scientific excellence.

More information:
https://mbg.au.dk

What we offer 
We offer:

• A unique opportunity to take an active role in establishing and shaping a growing proteomics research group at Aarhus University.
• Considerable scientific freedom to develop innovative technologies and pursue independent research ideas.
• Access to advanced mass spectrometry and proteomics research infrastructure.
• Opportunities to pioneer analytical workflows and establish technological capabilities with broad scientific applications.
• A research environment where technological innovation, scientific ambition, and independent initiative are strongly encouraged.
• Strong opportunities for high-impact scientific publications, international collaborations, and conference participation.
• Support for career development, scientific networking, and applications for independent research funding.
• Close interaction with national and international researchers working at the forefront of proteomics, PTM biology, and molecular biology.
• A collaborative and supportive environment that values scientific creativity, technical excellence, and intellectual curiosity.

Place of work and area of employment 
Department of Molecular Biology and Genetics, Aarhus University, Universitetsbyen 81, 8000 Aarhus C, Denmark.

Contact information
For further information, please contact:

Professor Michael L. Nielsen

Department of Molecular Biology and Genetics

Aarhus University

Email: mln@mbg.au.dk

Deadline
Applications must be received no later than 23 November 2026.

Application procedure
Shortlisting is used. This means that after the deadline for applications – and with the assistance from the assessment committee chairman, and the appointment committee if necessary, – the head of department selects the candidates to be evaluated. All applicants will be notified whether or not their applications have been sent to an expert assessment committee for evaluation. The selected applicants will be informed about the composition of the committee, and each applicant is given the opportunity to comment on the part of the assessment that concerns him/her self. 

Formalities and salary range
Natural Sciences refers to the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Danish Universities under the Danish Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation.

The application must be in English and include a curriculum vitae, degree certificate, a complete list of publications, a statement of future research plans and information about research activities, teaching portfolio and verified information on previous teaching experience (if any). Guidelines for applicants can be found here.

Appointment shall be in accordance with the collective labour agreement between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Further information on qualification requirements and job content may be found in the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Danish Universities.

Salary and terms as agreed between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Confederation of Professional Unions at basic salary steps 4-8.
